approach: Add one lexical gate step, `check_environment_reach(reading)`, in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs beside `check_code_survey` (3910), registered as one `step!` line directly after `step!(check_outcome_state(reading, request));` (3248). It returns Ok when capability is None or a question is set; a reading with no deliverables is still checked. Triggers: (A) a Create/Modify deliverable under `.github/workflows/`; (B) a host action in a Behavior criterion; (C) a records or history source in a Behavior criterion or the summary. Content criteria, assumptions, out_of_scope and the request are never scanned, so the `Environment:` repair text cannot trigger its own check. A triggered reading needs one `Environment:` assumption with a site word, a permission word and a data word. For B with a local-type site (local, producer, snapshot, checkout, copy) it also needs a no/without/missing-origin case. For C it needs a source word plus a counted figure or a reachable data/doc file path in the same assumption. Tokeniser (revised for this round): remove apostrophes first (job's becomes jobs); keep per token its original case so `PR`, `PRs` and `CI` can be matched case-sensitively before lowercasing; backticked spans kept only for command forms (`git push|fetch|clone|pull|remote`, `gh pr|api|run|auth|workflow|release|issue`) and `athena/records`; bare `api.github.com` kept as one word; every other backticked span and every bare token with `/`, `_`, `::` or an interior `.` is a break marker. Phrase windows never cross a break. B phrases (all windows count words, either side unless stated): `git`+push/fetch/clone/pull/remote; `gh`+command word; push verb with origin/remote/upstream/branch(es)/ref(s) within 4; fetch/clone/pull verb with origin/remote/upstream within 3 after (not `pull request`); `pull request(s)` with open/create/raise/submit/merge/push forms within 3; NEW (finding 1) case-sensitive token `PR`/`PRs` with open/opens/opened/create/raise/merge/reuse/push forms within 4; NEW 'GitHub API', 'host API' or `api.github.com` with call/calls/called/query/queries/use/uses/using/fetch/fetches within 3; NEW case-sensitive `CI` followed within 3 words by write/writes/written/push/pushes/commit/commits. C phrases: job records, job history, commit history, git history, git log, records branch, `athena/records` (bare or backticked), each with a source verb (from, use, uses, using, read, reads, counts, measures, replays, queries, parses, scans) within 3 words before; NEW (finding 3) the single words `history` and `records` also count, with a source verb within 3 words before, except `history` followed by `of`. 'in', 'citing' and 'reading' are not source verbs, so writes ('written in the records branch') and this job's criterion 4 do not trigger. The rule line in READING_RULES, the CHANGELOG entry, the doc comment (root cause: no step asking who performs each action, where, with what permissions, and what data it reaches; jobs 20261024-220048-engm, 20261025-070538-8ra0, 20261025-034247-nm0k) and corpus cases follow. The 8% share is declared as an unmeasured estimate with its basis.

decisions.choice: Cover the PR, GitHub API and CI-write wordings as host-action triggers (answers finding 1), using case-sensitive tokens for `PR`/`PRs` and `CI`, with apostrophes removed before tokenising.
decisions.reason: HISTORY.txt:1433 gives job 8ra0's own subject as "Open the job's PR early at verification start"; lines 906, 1376 and 1453 also use PR, and the 8ra0 introspection framed the class as any action that calls an external host. Without these rules the exact failing job is accepted. Removing apostrophes makes "opens the job's PR" four words (opens the jobs PR), inside the window of 4. Case-sensitive `PR` keeps lowercase `pr` in `pr.rs`, `gh pr` handled by the command rule, and words like 'pro' out; path and identifier tokens are break markers so gh/early.rs and `pr.rs` still do not fire. `CI` followed by a write verb catches CI-site actions named without a workflow deliverable ('the CI job writes the records'). The Environment assumption is never scanned, so naming CI there cannot trigger.

rejected.option: Match lowercase 'pr' as a word
rejected.why: Fires on `pr.rs`, 'gh pr' prose and many unrelated words after splitting.

rejected.option: Leave PR and API wording to the reader's judgement
rejected.why: That is the gap the class names; the 8ra0 shape would be accepted.

decisions.choice: Scan Behavior criteria for host actions and records sources, the summary for records sources only, and the deliverable list for workflows. Do not scan Content criteria, assumptions, out_of_scope or the request.
decisions.reason: A Behavior criterion is the one that must be run, so that is where an action or measurement is assigned (CriterionKind has only Content and Behavior). A workflow deliverable is a real CI assignment. The summary is read for C only because job nm0k cited records in its summary; the summary of this job says 'assumed CI writes', which must not fire the CI rule. Skipping assumptions keeps the repair text from triggering its own check.

rejected.option: Scan every criterion with bare-word triggers
rejected.why: Fires on gh/early.rs, parse_remote and 'entries are pushed onto the list'.

rejected.option: Trigger on the request text
rejected.why: A request can mention push without the reading assigning it.

decisions.choice: Match both active and passive forms and read backticked command forms; treat paths, identifiers and non-command backticks as break markers.
decisions.reason: Each refuse fixture traces to one rule (fixture map in the demonstrations). Commands are written in backticks, so dropping them would lose the real signal. Breaks keep gh/early.rs, parse_remote and this job's 'push/pull-request/gh' from matching.

rejected.option: Drop all backticked spans
rejected.why: Loses `gh pr create` and `git push`.

rejected.option: Whole-token match on push, origin, remote, gh
rejected.why: Splitting paths and identifiers yields those words.

rejected.option: Substring match
rejected.why: 'originates' would match 'origin'.

decisions.choice: Records sources include the single words `history` and `records` when a source verb is within 3 words before, and `history of` is excluded (answers finding 3).
decisions.reason: The reading's trigger design says 'job records, history or the records branch'; 'Use the figures from history' must be refused. The verb requirement keeps 'the history of the page', 'written in the records branch' and 'a reading citing job records' accepted. A source separated from its verb by more than 3 words ('measures the past readings in records') is a stated limit; the fixture 'The audit counts readings in records' (distance 3) is refused and the limit is in the doc comment.

rejected.option: Treat any occurrence of 'history' or 'records' as a source
rejected.why: Fires on 'the history of the page' and on writes; would refuse this job's own criterion 4.

rejected.option: Window of 5 words
rejected.why: Starts matching unrelated verbs far from the noun, such as 'reads the file ... records'.

decisions.reason: 'in' also fits writes; the class is reads and measurements of data the site may not reach. Fixture 'The record is written in the records branch' accepts.

rejected.option: Keep 'in' as a source verb
rejected.why: Demands quoted figures for a write.

decisions.choice: The no-origin case is required only when the Environment assumption names a local-type site. It is satisfied by the word 'origin' with one of no, without, missing, absent, none, non, always, lacks.
decisions.reason: A CI job always has an origin; the 8ra0 gap was a local or producer run with no origin or a non-GitHub origin.

rejected.option: Require a no-origin case for every host action
rejected.why: Forces filler when the site is CI.

decisions.choice: Reachable-file alternative for C: a raw token that contains `/`, has an extension md, json, jsonl, csv or txt, and does not start with records/ or athena/records. Existence is left to `check_reading_references`.
decisions.reason: `check_reading_references` scans assumptions (reading.rs:3148-3151) and refuses a path whose top directory is in the snapshot or KNOWN_TOP_DIRS and that does not exist and is not created. Paths under another top directory are not verified; the doc comment states this limit.

rejected.option: Accept any file with an allowed extension including .rs
rejected.why: crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs would satisfy a records-figure rule.

rejected.option: Pass repo_files into the new check
rejected.why: Duplicates `check_reading_references`.

decisions.choice: Counted figure for C: 1 to 5 digits directly before job(s), reading(s), commit(s), record(s), run(s), plan(s), introspection(s), attempt(s), case(s) or percent, or digits directly before `%`, in the same Environment assumption as a source word (records, history, log, logs, commits, branch).
decisions.reason: A year or a count of refs is not a quoted records figure.

rejected.option: Any 1 to 5 digit number
rejected.why: A bare year passes.

decisions.choice: No empty-deliverable gate: return Ok only when capability is None or a question is set.
decisions.reason: A capability reading may list no deliverables (reading.rs:2772 refuses only a retry for that) and still assign a measurement from job records, the engm and nm0k class.

rejected.option: Gate on deliverables.is_empty() as check_governance_coverage does (3316)
rejected.why: Skips measurement-only readings, which are part of the class.

decisions.choice: Place `step!(check_environment_reach(reading));` directly after `check_outcome_state`. Workflow corpus cases carry the Create deliverable, a Content criterion naming it, and a request that names no governance path.
decisions.reason: `check_governance_coverage` (3326-3331) refuses an unnamed workflow deliverable first. After outcome_state keeps the test `check_outcome_state_doc_names_root_cause_and_scope` (7725) and the corpus anchor `step!(check_reading_references(` unchanged.

rejected.option: Place it before governance
rejected.why: Breaks the ordering that test pins.

decisions.choice: Slice the CHANGELOG and the doc comment robustly (answers finding 2). CHANGELOG: take the text from the line `## [Unreleased]` to the next line starting `## [`; split it into items at lines starting `- `; collapse white space inside each item; pick the one item that contains the needle 'no step asking who performs each action, where, with what permissions, and what data it reaches' (the needle may straddle a wrapped line, so it is searched after collapsing); assert the other needles in that item only. Doc comment: cut `include_str!("reading.rs")` at `pub fn check_environment_reach`, take the preceding contiguous `///` lines, strip the leading `///` from each line, then collapse white space.
decisions.reason: CHANGELOG.md:12-30 shows entries wrapped at about 115 columns on indented continuation lines, so a ~100-character needle can straddle a break; the first line of an entry also begins with '- '. Splitting by item then collapsing removes both problems. Stripping `///` markers is needed because the doc comment lines would otherwise inject '///' into the needle. Item-level selection stops older entries that already say 'higher refusal rate is intended' from satisfying the test.

rejected.option: Start the slice at the line holding the phrase
rejected.why: Fails when the phrase wraps or the line begins with '- '.

rejected.option: Search the whole CHANGELOG
rejected.why: Older entries match.

decisions.choice: Declare 'expected 8% of newly refused readings' as an estimate that was not measured, with basis: no records in the snapshot to replay; 11 lines of HISTORY.txt name `.github/workflows` (about 5% of 200 commits); the host-action, PR/API and records triggers add a small allowance.
decisions.reason: The criterion text fixes 8%; nothing was measured.

rejected.option: State 8% as measured
rejected.why: Nothing was measured.

risks.risk: Lexical triggers miss an action in other words or catch a prose mention in a Behavior criterion; the 8% share is an unmeasured estimate.
risks.mitigation: Triggers need a verb-plus-target phrase and skip path, identifier and non-command backticked tokens; fixtures pin both sides, including this job's own criteria; the doc comment and CHANGELOG label 8% as an estimate with its basis and list the missed shapes as limits.

risks.risk: Case-sensitive `PR` and `CI` miss lowercase 'pr' written in prose, and the single words `history`/`records` can catch a read of an unrelated 'records' (for example a module name).
risks.mitigation: Prose names a pull request as 'pull request' or 'PR' in this repository (HISTORY.txt:906, 1376, 1433, 1453). Identifier and path tokens are breaks, so `records.rs` and records/ paths do not fire. The repair is one assumption line, and the accept fixtures 'the history of the page' and 'written in the records branch' pin the false-positive edge.

risks.risk: This job's own accepted summary or criteria hold a phrase that trips the new check.
risks.mitigation: A test copies the criterion and summary texts from the brief into an accept fixture; I traced criterion 4 ('citing job records, history or the records branch': no source verb) and the summary ('assumed CI writes' is not scanned in the summary; 'unreachable records' has no verb).

risks.risk: The word lists can be met by a wrong sentence.
risks.mitigation: The check makes the reader state site, permission and data; the doc says it is lexical, as for the `Code survey:` rule. The figure rule needs a counted noun and the file rule excludes records paths and code files.

risks.risk: Existing tests or fixtures that accept workflow-deliverable or action-bearing readings fail once the step exists.
risks.mitigation: Plan step 5 edits the two known tests; the workspace run finds any other, which gets an `Environment:` assumption.

risks.risk: A corpus refuse case is refused by an earlier check (criteria evidence, governance, references) and does not exercise the new step.
risks.mitigation: Workflow cases include a Content criterion naming the workflow path and a request that names no governance path; accept cases use only docs/guide.md and docs/design/roadmap.md from `repo_files()`; the producer checks the refusing check name for each refuse case.

risks.risk: The rule line exceeds the 220-byte cap or the section bound in briefs.rs.
risks.mitigation: The draft is about 205 bytes with the `- ` prefix; the producer measures it and sets the section bound just above.

risks.risk: New code or comment text trips the boundary scan or the personal-data allow-list.
risks.mitigation: CI and host vocabulary only, no banned phrases, no email-like text; the workspace run includes the scan.

demonstrations.method: Unit test in reading.rs `mod tests` that reads source text. Doc comment: split `include_str!("reading.rs")` at `pub fn check_environment_reach`, take the contiguous `///` lines before it, strip the leading `///` of each line, collapse white space. CHANGELOG: take `include_str!("../../../CHANGELOG.md")` from `## [Unreleased]` to the next `## [` line, split into items at lines starting `- `, collapse white space per item, pick the one item containing 'no step asking who performs each action, where, with what permissions, and what data it reaches'. In both texts assert: that phrase, '20261024-220048-engm', '20261025-070538-8ra0', '20261025-034247-nm0k', 'higher refusal rate is intended', 'expected 8% of newly refused readings' and 'estimate'.

demonstrations.method: Unit tests `environment_reach_*` in reading.rs `mod tests`, calling `refusing_check` (3226) and `check_environment_reach` directly (guards: capability set, no question). Refuse with no `Environment:` assumption, asserting the refusing check name is `check_environment_reach` and the error starts 'the reading was refused because': (i) Create `.github/workflows/lint.yml` plus a Content criterion naming it; (ii) one Behavior criterion each: 'Athena pushes the job branch to origin', 'The job branch is pushed to the remote', 'A pull request is opened on the remote', 'The pull request is opened with `gh pr create`', a bare `git push` backtick; (iii) NEW for finding 1: "Athena opens the job's PR at verification start", "Open the job's PR early at verification start", 'land calls the GitHub API to reuse the early PR', 'The check calls the GitHub API for the run status', 'The CI job writes the records'. Accept the same readings with 'Environment: the CI job has write permission to refs on the GitHub origin' for CI-site cases; for a local-site case ('the local Athena working copy has write access to the repo; with no origin or a non-GitHub origin it skips the push; with a GitHub origin it can push refs') `refusing_check` returns None. Also: an assumption missing the permission word is refused and the error names 'permissions'; a local-site assumption without the no-origin case is refused; a CI-site assumption without it is accepted; the label matches after trim and in any case; an assumption that only mentions 'environment' does not count; a Delete of a workflow does not trigger. Accept fixtures for finding 1: Behavior criteria that contain `pr.rs`, gh/early.rs, lowercase 'pr', 'express' and 'CIty' do not trigger.
demonstrations.observes: A workflow deliverable, or a push, pull-request, PR, GitHub API or CI-write action in a Behavior criterion, without a complete `Environment:` assumption is refused by `check_environment_reach`; with one, `refusing_check` gives None.
demonstrations.fails_without: With the `step!` line removed, `refusing_check` returns None for the refused readings and the check-name assertions fail. With the label or word lists wrong, the accept assertions fail. With the PR/API/CI rules removed, the three finding-1 fixtures are accepted and fail.

demonstrations.method: Unit tests `environment_reach_source_*` in reading.rs, each also run through `refusing_check` to assert the refusing check's name. Three readings shaped like the three jobs. (engm) a code reading with a `Code survey:` assumption naming a crates/ path (so `check_code_survey` passes) and the Behavior criterion 'The history check reads the job records on the records branch': refused with no Environment assumption; refused with a site, permission and data assumption that quotes no figure and lists no file (error says to quote figures inline or name a reachable file); accepted with 'Environment: the CI job has read-only access to contents and cannot write the records branch; it sees 3 jobs and 12 readings'. (8ra0) the push/origin/PR reading of criterion 3, accepted only with a complete assumption. (nm0k) a docs reading whose summary says 'Use the figures from job records and history': refused; accepted when the assumption quotes '3 jobs' or '40%' or lists `docs/design/roadmap.md`; refused when the only file is `records/foo.json`, `athena/records/x.json` or `crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs`, or the only number is a year. NEW for finding 3: summary 'Use the figures from history' refused; Behavior 'The audit counts readings in records' refused; accepted with quoted figures. Accept: 'the history of the page' (with and without 'reads' before it), 'The record is written in the records branch', 'a reading citing job records', a reading with no deliverables and no source verb. A reading with no deliverables and a records-source Behavior criterion is refused. A loop covers every phrase (job records, job history, commit history, git history, git log, records branch, athena/records bare and in backticks, single `history`, single `records`), each with a source verb.
demonstrations.observes: A reading that cites records or history as a source is refused unless figures are quoted inline next to a counted noun or a reachable data or doc file is listed, and is accepted when they are. Three differently shaped readings plus the single-word forms are covered, so the class is tested.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the step, `refusing_check` returns None for the refused readings and the name assertions fail. Without the figure and file rule, the 'complete but nothing quoted', bare-year and records-only-file readings are wrongly accepted. Without the single-word rule, 'from history' is accepted and fails.

demonstrations.method: Plan step 6 adds fifteen cases to `reading_check_cases()` (refusal_corpus.rs:668) using `case(..)` and `base_reading` (exist, 186 and 117). Refuse, `Expected::Refuse("check_environment_reach")`: environment-ci-workflow-without-an-environment (Create `.github/workflows/lint.yml` plus a Content criterion naming it), environment-host-action-without-an-environment ('Athena pushes the job branch to origin'), environment-pr-without-an-environment ("Athena opens the job's PR at verification start"), environment-github-api-without-an-environment ('The check calls the GitHub API for the run status'), environment-ci-write-without-an-environment ('The CI job writes the records'), environment-records-source-without-figures ('The history check reads the job records on the records branch'), environment-bare-history-source-without-figures (summary 'Use the figures from history'), environment-records-source-with-a-bare-year (Environment names only a year). Accept: environment-ci-workflow-with-an-environment, environment-host-action-with-origin-cases, environment-records-source-with-quoted-figures, environment-records-source-with-a-reachable-file (lists docs/design/roadmap.md, in `repo_files()`), environment-trigger-words-only-inside-other-words (dash-bullet request naming push to origin, which becomes Content criteria, plus a Behavior criterion with 'originates', a gh/early.rs path, `parse_remote`, 'entries are pushed onto the list', a Vec push), environment-gh-module-path-only, environment-pr-inside-paths-only (`pr.rs`, gh/early.rs, 'the history of the page', 'written in the records branch'). Input-form map (ids read in the file: code-reading-without-a-survey 689, code-reading-with-a-survey 700, design-reading-without-existing-code 738, request-names-a-governance-file-the-reading-ignores 772, delivery-request-naming-a-workflow-fails-governance-first 393, full-deliverable-path 802, boundary-word-in-a-deliverable-path 890; star-bullets 542, numbered-dot-parts 554): workflow Create/Modify -> the two workflow cases; Delete -> unit test only (the governance behavior for a deleted workflow was not read); push, pull-request, PR, GitHub API, CI-write phrases -> the host-action cases; records source with a figure, a file, a year, bare history -> the records cases; slash-joined, path and identifier tokens, words inside other words, PR inside paths -> the accept cases; dash bullets -> the trigger-words case; star and numbered bullets reach the gate only as Content criteria through `base_reading`, which the check does not scan, and are covered by the existing bullet cases. Six new `INPUT_FORMS` tags: ci-workflow-deliverable, host-action-criterion, records-source-citation, environment-assumption, trigger-word-inside-other-word, pr-or-api-wording (length 23 to 29), each carried by a case. Add `environment_reach_refusal_is_declared_intended`. I have not run the suite and cite no result.

demonstrations.method: Unit tests `environment_reach_accepts_*` in reading.rs plus the corpus accept cases. A plain docs reading (`governed_reading(&["docs/x.md"], &["docs/x.md exists"], &[])`) passes `check_environment_reach` and `refusing_check` returns None. Accepted with no `Environment:`: Content criteria naming push, origin, gh/early.rs, parse_remote, PR, 'the history of the page'; Behavior criteria containing only 'fixed where it originates', 'ghost', 'pushdown', 'remotely', 'Vec push', 'entries are pushed onto the list', 'The record is written in the records branch', a `pr.rs` path; this job's own criteria 3 to 7 and its summary text copied from the brief; a push or PR phrase in an assumption or in out_of_scope only; a decline (capability None); a reading with a question. The 8% estimate is pinned by the criterion 1 and 5 declaration tests.
demonstrations.observes: Docs-only readings and readings without an assigned action or a records source are accepted. Words in paths, identifiers, Content criteria and other words do not trigger.
demonstrations.fails_without: With substring or bare-token triggers, 'originates', gh/early.rs and parse_remote are refused and the accept tests fail. Without the capability and question guards, the decline and question readings are refused.
